en: The Therāpadāna: Chapter on Those Who Honored the Pile of Firewood (Citakapūjakavagga) 10. The Apadāna of the Elder Anusaṃsāvaka [Verse 1] "O Bhikkhu, you who have gone forth in the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa, I shall speak of your former conduct; listen with undistracted mind. [Verse 2] In the dispensation of the Buddha Padumuttara, I was a brahmin named Uttara, well-versed in the three Vedas. [Verse 3] Having heard the fame of that Blessed One, I went to the presence of the Teacher, desiring to see him. [Verse 4] There I saw the Buddha, the Great Sage, Resplendent like the rising sun, shining with a halo of one fathom. [Verse 5] Having seen the Teacher, the Supreme among Men, I paid homage at his feet and sat down to one side. [Verse 6] Then the Teacher, knowing my inclination, Expounded the Dhamma to me, causing the hair on my body to stand on end. [Verse 7] Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I made this aspiration for the sake of future benefit: [Verse 8] ‘May I, having heard such a Dhamma as this, Attain the supreme fruit of Arahantship. [Verse 9] When I had thus made my aspiration, The Teacher, the Knower of the World, spoke these words:

[Verse 10] ‘This man, having made an aspiration, Will attain the supreme fruit of Arahantship. [Verse 11] After passing through many hundred thousand aeons, He will become a Buddha named Gotama. [Verse 12] Having reached the age of twenty-nine years, He will renounce the world and go forth into homelessness. [Verse 13] Under the Bodhi tree of the Aśvattha, He will realize the unsurpassed state of Buddhahood. [Verse 14] Having become a Buddha, he will set in motion The Wheel of Dhamma that has never been turned before. [Verse 15] Having established the supreme Dispensation, He will lead many thousands of beings to final Nibbāna. [Verse 16] And when that Blessed One has passed away, His relics will be honored by gods and humans alike. [Verse 17] And when that Blessed One has passed away, A stupa of gold and silver will be erected for him. [Verse 18] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will pay homage there with perfumes and garlands. [Verse 19] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will offer lamps and incense at that place. [Verse 20] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will offer food and drink at that place. [Verse 21] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will offer clothing and bedding at that place. [Verse 22] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will offer medicine and requisites at that place. [Verse 23] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will perform various acts of service there. [Verse 24] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will build monasteries and dwellings there. [Verse 25] And when that Blessed One has passed away, People will maintain the Dispensation with great care. [Verse 26] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The true Dhamma will endure for five hundred years. [Verse 27] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The counterfeit Dhamma will endure for five hundred years. [Verse 28] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The true Dhamma will gradually disappear. [Verse 29] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The counterfeit Dhamma will gradually disappear. [Verse 30] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be shrouded in darkness and confusion. [Verse 31] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be filled with suffering and lamentation. [Verse 32] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be devoid of the Three Jewels. [Verse 33] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be subject to birth, aging, and death. [Verse 34] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be swept away by the flood of saṃsāra. [Verse 35] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without refuge or protection. [Verse 36] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a leader or guide. [Verse 37] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a teacher or instructor. [Verse 38] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a refuge or shelter. [Verse 39] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a light or illumination. [Verse 40] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a lamp or torch. [Verse 41] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a sun or moon. [Verse 42] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a jewel or treasure. [Verse 43] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a lotus or lily. [Verse 44] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a fragrance or scent. [Verse 45] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a flower or fruit. [Verse 46] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a tree or forest. [Verse 47] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a mountain or peak. [Verse 48] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a river or stream. [Verse 49] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a lake or pond. [Verse 50] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a well or spring. [Verse 51] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a cloud or rain.

[Verse 52] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a breeze or wind. [Verse 53] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a fire or heat. [Verse 54] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a coolness or shade. [Verse 55] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a path or way. [Verse 56] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a vehicle or carriage. [Verse 57] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a boat or ship. [Verse 58] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a bridge or ford. [Verse 59] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a gate or door. [Verse 60] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a wall or fence. [Verse 61] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a pillar or support. [Verse 62] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a foundation or base. [Verse 63] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a root or source. [Verse 64] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a beginning or end. [Verse 65] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a limit or boundary. [Verse 66] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a center or middle. [Verse 67] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a circumference or edge. [Verse 68] And when that Blessed One has passed away, The world will be without a horizon
While wandering for alms,
I saw the Victor Vipassi;
I offered him a spoonful of food.
To that Tathāgata, the Lord of bipeds,
I then paid homage with a clear heart and a joyful mind.
I exhorted the Buddha for the sake of attaining the supreme goal.
Ninety-one aeons ago,
I exhorted [others];
I do not know a state of woe,
for such is the fruit of exhortation.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Anusaṃsāvaka spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Anusaṃsāvaka.
The thirtieth chapter, the Citakapūjaka Vagga, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
The funeral pyre, the Pāricchattaka tree, the sound,
the Gosīsa sandalwood, and the spread of grass.
Pāda, Padesa, Saraṇa,
Amba, and Saṃsāvaka;
forty-eight verses in total.
These have been calculated by those possessed of analytical insight.
Now, the summary of the sections:
Kaṇikāra, Hatthidada.
The support, the water, and the seat; the quick-witted, the panegyrist,
and the lifting, and the head-pillow.
Paṇṇada and Citapūjī,
and all the verses as well;
here [there are] four hundred.
And exactly fifty-one;
five hundred and twenty-five in total,
seventy-two more than that.
The number of apadānas of Tiṭṭha has been calculated by the seers of meaning.
This is the Kaṇikāra Chapter Ten.
The Third Hundred is completed.
